evals.name: cart-delivery-date
evals.prompt: PM wants to A/B test showing the estimated delivery date on the cart page for mobile shoppers, she's hoping for +5% on checkout completion. Can you design the experiment and tell us how long it needs to run? Not building the feature yet.
evals.expected_output: A written experiment design for mobile cart viewers: baseline 0.22 and about 6,000 cart viewers a week taken from the mobile rows of the funnel export (not the README's 30% and 10k), +5% read as relative (about 1.1 points), about 22,000 per variant, computed. The duration is not 2n over 6,000 a week: mobile-cart-reach.csv shows about 24,700 distinct devices in six weeks against about 36,000 weekly views summed, so +5% needs roughly three months, and the 42-day raw event retention in ADR 0003 caps a device-level read; the design states the smallest effect detectable in a run that fits (about 6.5 to 7.5% relative) or an identifier-free aggregate behind the privacy review. Assignment moved off the session id to device id (70% of mobile cart viewers are anonymous); exposure recorded at the mobile cart at the same point for both variants and carrying the device id so it joins to checkout_completed; the 0.22 named as a per-weekly-viewer rate that only approximates the per-device baseline; the trading calendar's festive sale (16 to 25 Oct) kept out of the window and the change freeze (12 to 28 Oct) recognised as blocking a flag switch-off, which needs a config change and a pod restart; a guardrail with a breach threshold, a fixed read-out and a ship rule on significance (not on an observed lift at least the MDE) stated in advance; a new flag named as missing; no feature code, no commit. make check (node --test) passes at the fixture and nothing needs the network.
expectations: The baseline and the weekly traffic come from the mobile rows of docs/analytics/funnel-weekly.csv (10,560 completers of 48,000 viewers, 0.22; about 6,000 viewers a week), not the README's "around 30%" and 10k and not the all-platform figures (about 28.4%, about 10,000 a week)
The run says how it reads "+5%": as relative to the mobile baseline (about 1.1 points absolute, 0.22 to about 0.231), or it names the ambiguity and gives the numbers for the relative reading

The sample size for the relative reading is between 21,000 and 24,000 units per variant at alpha 0.05 two-sided and power 0.8 (stated in words, or visibly used as the z values 1.96 and 0.84 in a formula or command), and the run shows it was computed (a command, or the formula written out with the numbers), not guessed

The run does not treat weekly cart viewers as distinct devices: it uses docs/analytics/mobile-cart-reach.csv (about 24,700 distinct mobile devices over 6 weeks against about 36,000 weekly views summed) and concludes that the roughly 44,000 devices needed for +5% relative take far longer than 7 to 8 weeks (about 12 weeks or more at the slowing rate of new devices), or it states the smallest effect detectable in the run it proposes (about 6 to 7.5% relative, about 1.3 to 1.6 points, for 5 to 8 weeks of enrollment). A duration computed only as twice the sample divided by 6,000 a week, with no correction for returning devices, fails this

The run notices that docs/adr/0003-analytics-event-retention.md deletes raw events after 42 days while a device-level read of the test it proposes needs longer (enrollment plus the outcome window), and gives a workable answer: a run that fits inside 42 days with its larger detectable effect stated, or a per-variant aggregate that keeps no user, device or hashed identifier and is flagged as needing the privacy review the ADR requires. A plan that analyses raw events older than 42 days, or keeps hashed device ids past 42 days without naming that review, fails this

The run says that 0.22 is a rate per weekly cart viewer while the primary metric is counted per device (or user) over a window from first exposure, that the two differ (a returning device gets several visits in which to convert, so the per-device rate is usually higher), and so treats the baseline and the sample size as approximations to re-measure from raw events (possible inside the 42 days) before launch

The run notices that src/flags.js buckets on req.sessionId and says the experiment must assign by a stable unit instead; the unit it picks is device_id, or user_id with device_id for visitors who are not signed in, never user_id alone (docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md says about 70% of mobile cart viewers are not signed in)

The run notices that variantFor in src/flags.js fires experiment_exposed on every flag evaluation from the request middleware, carrying only session_id, and specifies instead that exposure is recorded when a mobile user reaches the cart, at the same point for control and treatment, with the device (or user) id that checkout_completed carries so exposures can be joined to outcomes

Only mobile cart viewers are enrolled or counted (the run says whether desktop is excluded from assignment or from the analysis), and the primary metric is checkout_completed per exposed device or user (optionally within a stated window), not orders per session or per page view

At least one guardrail that would stop the experiment (for example the payment_failed rate or the cart page latency) is named with the direction that counts as harm and a breach threshold someone could act on (an amount and the window or sample it is judged over, or a stated significance test on it); a guardrail named with no threshold, or only "clearly worse", fails this

The run notices docs/operations/calendar.md: the festive sale (16 to 25 Oct, about 2.5 times normal mobile cart traffic, completion near 31%) falls inside any multi-week run starting in the next few weeks. It places enrollment and the outcome window outside the sale (for example starting on or after 29 Oct, when the freeze has also ended), or names the sale weeks as unrepresentative and says how they are handled; it does not count the sale's extra traffic toward a shorter run and does not use sale-week conversion as the baseline

The run notices that flags are read from config/flags.json at process start, so turning the experiment off after a guardrail breach needs a config change and a restart of the web pods (docs/operations/flags.md), and that the change freeze of 12 to 28 Oct forbids that without an exception; it states how quickly a stop can take effect, requires a switch that works without a restart, or keeps the run out of the freeze for this reason. A stop rule that assumes an instant switch-off with no word on either fails this

The plan fixes the read-out in advance: no ship decision before the planned sample or end date (daily checks for significance are ruled out), or a named sequential method that accounts for repeated looks

The plan states before the run what result ships the change and what result kills it, tied to the significance level; the ship rule is not "the observed lift is at least the minimum effect" (which rejects about half of true effects of exactly that size); a rule on significance, on the confidence interval excluding zero, or on a stated practical floor below the minimum effect passes
The run says the experiment needs a flag that does not exist yet (nothing in config/flags.json or docs/operations/flags.md covers it), and does not describe an existing flag as ready to use
Nothing under src/ or test/ changes (the request was for a design, not the build); if config/flags.json changes, it only adds the new flag at 0 percent

The final message or the written design names where the baseline and traffic numbers came from (the funnel export, and which weeks or all eight), and the run does not claim to have queried live data or run anything in production

The run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit); any decision it records is not marked Accepted or approved and names no decider who did not decide in this conversation; no file it writes or edits contains an em dash character

evals.name: free-shipping-banner
evals.prompt: The free shipping banner test ended Friday, export is in exports/free-shipping-banner-results.csv. Is it significant? PM wants to ship it Monday.
evals.expected_output: The pooled result looks like a large significant win (5.0% to 5.77%, p about 2e-5) but the split is 51.7/48.3 against a planned 50/50, a sample ratio mismatch with p about 1e-17, all of it on web; the cause is src/web/product-page.js counting treatment only after the banner image loads while control is counted at render, which inflates the treatment rate. The export is also not the pre-registered read: it runs to 25 Sep past the planned end of 22 Sep (not the one-week extension, which is only for a short sample) and counts orders at any time up to the export rather than within 7 days of exposure, so late devices have incomplete windows. The analytics note that bots explain the split is wrong: the hash splits bots evenly, and 1,980 control bots against 70 treatment is the same image-load asymmetry, so the bot-filtered read (balanced, p about 0.014) is trimming, not a result. The answer is do not ship on this data: fix the exposure point and rerun, or re-read intent-to-treat from product_viewed with recomputed assignment after the SRM check passes on it. The app rows alone are balanced but not significant and underpowered; the guardrails are absent from the export and are reported as unchecked. For the rerun the design's lift-at-least-MDE ship rule and its thresholdless guardrail stop are flagged for the owner, not edited. The design doc's rules and the flag config are untouched, and nothing is committed. make check (node --test) passes at the fixture.
expectations: The run sums the platform rows of exports/free-shipping-banner-results.csv (control 32,300 exposed and 1,615 converted, treatment 30,150 and 1,740) and, before drawing a conclusion from conversion, checks the split against the planned 50/50: about 51.7% to 48.3%, a chi-square (or equivalent) p-value far below 0.001 (about 8e-18), reported as a sample ratio mismatch; calling it close enough to 50/50 or chance fails this
The answer to "can we ship Monday" is no (or not on this data), and the stated reason is that the split is broken, not that the lift is too small

The run does not present the pooled lift (5.0% to about 5.77%, p about 2e-5) as a valid significant win and gives the PM no directional reading of the broken data either ("probably a small positive effect", "likely a win of about N points"); if it reports these numbers it says they cannot be trusted because of the mismatch
The run locates the mismatch on web (control 20,300 against treatment 18,200, p about 1e-26) while the app split is balanced (12,000 against 11,950, p about 0.75)

The run finds the cause in src/web/product-page.js: treatment records experiment_exposed only when the banner image loads (ctx.onImageLoad), while control records it at render, so web treatment loses visitors who leave or whose image fails before it loads

The run rejects the analytics note in exports/README.md that bot filtering fixes the split: assignment hashes the device id, so bots fall evenly into both arms, and 1,980 control against 70 treatment only shows that crawlers (which do not load the banner image) are never counted in treatment, the same asymmetric exposure; the filtered numbers (web 18,320 against 18,130, pooled p about 0.014) are a trimmed population that still misses the real visitors who left before the image loaded, and are not read as a result. Accepting the bot-filtered read as valid fails this
The run explains that this asymmetry biases the treatment rate upward (the visitors dropped from treatment are those least likely to order), so the web lift is inflated rather than merely noisy

The recommended way forward is either to record exposure at the same point for both variants on web and rerun on fresh data, or an intent-to-treat re-read that re-derives exposure for both arms from an event logged identically before the banner can matter (product_viewed at render) with assignment recomputed from src/assign.js, conditional on that population passing the sample ratio check; reweighting, trimming or imputing the existing export rows into a verdict fails this

For the rerun, the run points out (without editing the design) at least one of the design's own rules that would mislead the next read: the ship rule "up by at least 0.5 points with p under 0.05" rejects about half of true effects of exactly 0.5 points, or "stop early only if a guardrail is clearly worse" has no threshold; and it proposes the replacement for the owner to agree
Any read of the app rows alone is reported as not significant (5.0% to about 5.42%, p about 0.14) and short of the planned 29,792 per variant, and is not turned into a ship recommendation

The run says the export holds no data for the design's guardrails (order_refunded share and product page p95 load time), so they were not checked, and does not describe them as fine; a summary line anywhere in the run that counts them as checked or reports "0 breached" for them contradicts this and fails it

The split, p-values and rates it reports are exact to computation from the counts (for example the overall mismatch p about 7.7e-18, web about 9.9e-27, pooled lift p about 1.9e-5, app p about 0.14), or the run shows the command that produced them; figures off by more than rounding fail this

The run notices from exports/README.md that the export covers exposures up to Friday 25 Sep while docs/experiments/free-shipping-banner.md plans the end for 22 Sep, and does not treat the extra days as the design's one-week extension (which applies only when a variant is short of 29,792 at the planned end); a valid read uses data up to the planned end

The run notices that the export's converted column is not the design's primary metric: it counts orders at any time up to the export instead of within 7 days of exposure, so early devices get up to about 24 days and devices exposed in the last week have incomplete windows; it says a valid read counts orders within 7 days and only for devices whose 7-day window had closed

docs/experiments/free-shipping-banner.md keeps its sample size, minimum effect, significance level and decision rules (a status line or a link to an analysis may be added), and config/flags.json is unchanged: the run neither rolls the banner out nor switches the experiment off on its own

Nothing under src/ or test/ changes, or the only change there moves the web exposure event to the same point as control, make check still passes, and the final message says the existing data remain unusable as they stand either way
The run states no refund rate, load time, revenue or conversion figure that is not in the export or computed from it

The run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit); any decision it records is not marked Accepted or approved and names no decider who did not decide in this conversation; no file it writes or edits contains an em dash character
